terms.meaning: a number for how well confidence matched results, where lower is better
the app's rating for a fan's reads, as named in the code

sections.name: FormResult
sections.title: Recent form result type
sections.what: Defines the three possible results for a recent call: good, poor or none.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps form values to a fixed set so each has a symbol.
sections.watch_out: Any other value would have no symbol to show.

sections.name: TimingTowerEntry, FORM_TEXT
sections.title: Row data and form symbols
sections.what: Describes one leaderboard row: rank, name, rating, calibration score, calls this week, recent form and change in position. Maps each form result to a plus, a minus or a dot.
sections.why: Likely reason: these are the fields a timing tower shows. The symbols make form quick to read.
sections.watch_out: The calibration score is null when there are too few calls, and the row then shows a dash.

sections.name: TimingTowerRow
sections.title: Leaderboard row display
sections.what: Draws one row: rank, name with calls this week, calibration to three decimals or a dash, form symbols with a text summary, rating, and an arrow with the size of change or a dash for no change.
sections.why: Likely reason: a dense table where each number is useful at a glance.
sections.watch_out: The row relies on its parent being a list, so placing it elsewhere breaks the structure.

summary: One row of a leaderboard styled like a motor-racing timing tower, showing rank, name, rating, calibration, recent form and position change.
purpose: Lets a user see a fan's standing and recent record at a glance.
why: The comment describes a dense F1-style leaderboard row.
how: Reads the entry, works out whether the position went up, down or stayed, and draws the fields with their text labels, form symbols and arrow.
inputs: entry, a TimingTowerEntry object with rank, name, readRating, brier, callsThisWeek, form, and change.
risks: It must sit inside a list element or the markup is invalid. An empty form list still gets a label.
debug: If the row is missing, check that a parent list exists. If the arrow is wrong, check the sign of change. If the calibration shows a dash, the fan has too few calls.
